text: Slicing pulls out a whole range of items at once, using start colon end inside the square brackets.
[clear throat] Zero to three gives you the first three elements — indices zero, one, and two.
Here's the key rule: the start is included, but the end is not — it stops just before that index.
Omit the start and the slice runs from the very beginning of the list.
Omit the end and it runs all the way to the finish — a handy shortcut.
Add a second colon and a step value to skip items, [sniff] every second element here.
Here's a favorite trick: a step of negative one reverses the entire list, no special function needed.
Just like indexing, slicing works identically on strings, carving out substrings by position.
[groan] And you can even assign to a slice, replacing a whole chunk of the list in one clean move.
Up next, dictionaries. Comment the topic you want after that.
